description: Fleet-wide backup health for the platform team. Series: spec/05-observability.md §2; panel list: §7.

panels.title: Operator build
panels.description: Constant 1, always exported. If this reads No data the scrape is broken and every other 'No data' on this dashboard is meaningless rather than reassuring.

panels.title: Backup success ratio (range)
panels.description: Backups that produced restorable data: result completed OR partiallycompleted. PartiallyCompleted is a success with a hole — some volumes were skipped because their CSI cannot snapshot — so it does not belong in the failure count, but the hole is counted separately in *Backup outcomes by result* below.

panels.title: Namespaces with failed backups right now
Oldest successful backup — top 25

defaults.noValue: No backup series at all — check the scrape

panels.description: The fleet triage list: whoever is at the top has gone longest without a successful backup.

panels.title: Backup failures by namespace
panels.description: §7 calls this a heatmap. Grafana's heatmap panel needs numeric y-buckets and `namespace` is categorical, so the faithful rendering is a status history: one row per namespace, one cell per interval, coloured when a backup entered a failed phase. Rows only appear for namespaces that actually failed.

panels.title: Backup outcomes by result
panels.description: Four terminal results, not three: completed, partiallycompleted, partiallyfailed, failed. A rising partiallycompleted with a flat failure count is the quiet one — volumes being skipped because a storage class stopped being snapshottable, while every run still reports success.

panels.title: Time since last successful DR run
Namespaces matched vs failed
panels.description: Last-run gauges. matched dropping to 0 means the namespace selector stopped matching — a silent way to back up nothing while every run reports success.

panels.title: Movers: active, queued, limit
panels.description: A limit of 0 means unlimited. Queue depth pinned at a non-zero floor while active sits on the limit is saturation.

panels.title: Concurrency slot utilisation
panels.description: Meaningless when the limit is 0 (unlimited): the clamp makes it read as active/1.

panels.title: Repository state
panels.description: One row per repository, keyed by (location, scope, namespace). scope is cluster or namespace; namespace is empty for the shared cluster repo. size is the physical bytes in object storage — the only size measurement there is, and the one the bucket bills for (spec §2.11). Empty check/prune cells mean never measured; for prune that is normal on Immutable locations, which never prune by design (ADR 0005).

panels.title: Stale locks present vs reaped
panels.description: Reaping without the present count falling means locks are being re-created as fast as the reaper removes them.

panels.title: Repository size over time
panels.description: Physical bytes under each repository prefix (status.approximateSizeBytes) — the storage bill. A curve that only ever rises means prune is not reclaiming; cross-check the prune age in the table above.

panels.title: Discovery health
panels.description: Drives the DiscoveryFailed alert. 0 means Backup projections are drifting from the repository.

panels.title: Projected backups vs orphan snapshots
panels.description: Orphans are snapshot groups whose namespace no longer exists — DR data for gone namespaces, restorable only via ClusterRestore. Non-zero is not an error.

panels.title: Erasures blocked
panels.description: ClusterErasure objects waiting on an Immutable object-lock to expire (R21 / ADR 0005).

panels.title: Sync lag (snapshots behind)
panels.description: The series that matters. A sync can keep completing while falling further behind; only lag shows it (spec §2.12).

panels.title: Time since last successful sync
panels.description: A sync that never completed reports 0, not absent, so the ExternalSyncStale rule can fire on day one.

panels.title: Why there is no 'bytes copied' panel

options.content:
§7 asks for *bytes copied per sync*. There is no such series and there deliberately never was: `restic copy --json` emits no machine-readable summary, so `status.bytesCopied` stays 0 rather than carrying an invented figure (spec §2.12, ADR 0013).

A panel here would be a permanent flat zero, which reads as *nothing was copied* — worse than the absence. **Snapshots copied** and **lag** are the honest volume signals.

panels.title: Dynamic webhook denials
panels.description: The operator's dynamic webhook only. Static-rule denials are ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and land in the apiserver's own apiserver_validating_admission_policy_check_total (ADR 0010).

panels.title: Snapshot exposure wait p95
panels.description: Wait for a VolumeSnapshot to become ReadyToUse and its temp PVC to bind. A driver that takes minutes here pushes the whole backup window out.

panels.title: VolumeSnapshots per PVC — top 20
panels.description: Counts snapshots from ALL tools, an incumbent's included (ADR 0006). Above ~20 the ceph-csi flatten threshold becomes a real risk — this is the PVCSnapshotPileup signal.

panels.title: Reconcile errors by controller
panels.description: Inherited controller-runtime registry (spec §2.10) — not a crystalbackup_ series.

panels.title: Workqueue depth
panels.description: A depth that never drains is a wedged controller.
